text:
Maria: Heads up — seeing a perf regression on Llama3-13B after the kernel-selector v3.4 roll. p99 latency up ~18% on small chat workloads, mainly in KV/cache paths.

Jake: Can you repro locally and share logs?

Maria: Quick repro on staging. Attaching perf summary (see s3 path below). Key observations: KV cache evict spikes, extra memcpy time, batcher producing more micro-batches at seq 64-128. Selector is picking an FP16 vectorized kernel that looks fast in isolation but causes bad alignment for our KV layout.

InfraBot: Deploy 2026-03-17T21:02 - kernel-selector v3.4 rolled.

Omar: Paste the exact config you used for the repro?

Maria: Sure — minimal snippet:

```yaml
model: llama-3-13b
rope_theta: 0.7
hidden_size: 8192
num_heads: 64
rmsnorm: true
kernel_selector: auto
batching:
  max_tokens: 1024
  prefer_latency: true
```

Maria: Profiling flamegraph shows big time in `kv_cache_read` + `memcpy_aligned` around the attention path. Hotspot when head_dim=128 (8192/64). RMSNorm path chooses SiLU-enabled FFN kernel which changes how tensors are laid out in intermediate buffers.

Lena: My guess: rope_theta=0.7 interacts with our legacy RoPE index math and causes non-contiguous access pattern for KV indices, producing extra cache copies. Vectorized kernel expects contiguous, aligned buffers — so it falls back to slower path or forces copies.

Ravi: Another angle: kernel selector heuristics include heuristics for head_dim * num_heads alignment. If alignment != 256 or 512 boundary, some intrinsics are disabled. That could explain sudden memcpy. Need metrics: bytes_per_head alignment and selected kernel id.

Jake: Can you run two quick A/Bs: (A) pin `kernel_selector: kernel_v2` (older scalar-friendly kernel) (B) force `rope_theta: 1.0` and see delta?

Maria: I ran those:
- baseline (auto / rope_theta 0.7): p99 132ms
- kernel_v2 forced: p99 110ms (−16%)
- rope_theta 1.0: p99 124ms (−6%)
- rope_theta 0.5: p99 129ms (−2%)
So kernel pinning has the biggest effect. rope_theta moves it a bit.

Omar: Interesting. That points to selector choosing a vectorized GEMM that is fast for compute but pays for copies on our layout.

Lena: Action items:
- Add guard in kernel-selector to avoid vectorized kernel when head_dim*num_heads byte stride not aligned to 64 or 128.
- Add batching heuristic: if seq_len in (60,100) and model variant Llama-3-13b, prefer smaller micro-batches to reduce KV churn.
- Add perf test for head_count/head_dim combos in our CI perf harness.

Jake: I'll open a small PR to add the selector guard + metric emission (kernel_id, chosen_reason). Tagging @InfraBot for canary rollout.

InfraBot: Canary created: canary/rope-kernel-186-2026-03-18.

Ravi: Also double-check chat template assumptions — many chat templates add a ~20 token system prompt. That pushes typical user requests from 60->80 tokens into the problematic window.

Maria: Good call. I'll add targeted evals with prompt sets at 50/70/90 tokens. If we confirm, we could consider bumping default rope_theta for Llama-3-family or add compatibility layer.

Lena: Note: changing default rope_theta is a product-affecting change; prefer runtime selector fixes first.

Jake: For Dedicated customers we can route Llama-3-13b to kernel_v2 as a short-term mitigation. We should avoid changing shipped defaults until we have regression test coverage.

Maria: Uploading traces and perf dumps to s3: s3://redwood-perf/1857502468/traces.zip. Will follow up with flamegraphs and a small repro script.

Omar: Thanks — will triage tomorrow and prioritize selector guard.

Lena: I'll add a note in the runtime ops dashboard to watch KV eviction rate and kernel_id distribution.

Jake: Assigning follow-ups: #1 run expanded A/B across nu variants; #2 add selector guard PR; #3 add perf CI tests.

Maria: Thanks everyone. I'll post updates in this thread as I get traces processed. :thumbsup:
